statement_summary: The group must maintain one information security program aligned to NIST CSF 2.0
The Group CISO is accountable for the program and the Group OT Security Director for OT security across divisions
Each division and corporate must complete a risk analysis at least annually and after major changes, using NIST SP 800-30 Rev
Risk acceptance authority: Low, the division security and compliance lead; Moderate, the division president; High, the Group Chief Risk Officer...

Security policies, procedures, risk analyses, assessments, and compliance evidence must be retained for at least 6 years, or longer where a...
AI systems
Workforce members who violate security policies must be sanctioned in proportion to intent and harm, and HR must document every sanction
Every user must have a unique identity in SYS-G1
Access must be role-based and least privilege
MFA is required for all workforce access to business systems
No direct IT-to-OT paths
Service accounts that cross an OT DMZ must be read-only, serve one division, and be documented in an interconnection agreement
Termination
Managers and data owners must certify access every quarter, including privileged, service, and local OT accounts
Privileged access must be granted just in time through PAM, with approval and session recording
Accounts must lock after 10 failed attempts
Vendor and integrator remote access must go through group PAM with named accounts, MFA, approval for each session, recording, and OT sensor...
Device credentials
Emergency access
External identities
Every workforce member must report a suspected incident to the group SOC within 1 hour of noticing it
The SOC must handle incidents using one group severity scale and the group playbooks, including the P08 runbook
Operations decide on operations
The incident log must record the time each clock starts: confirmed discovery (PHMSA), knowledge of a discharge (EPA), determination of a...
The Group General Counsel must maintain the multi-regulator notification matrix (P08) and review it every quarter
Printed copies of the notification matrix, contacts, and forms must be kept at the IOC, BCC, GCC, PCC, and backup PCC, so notices can be made when...
SEC materiality
Ransom payments require board risk committee approval, counsel, the cyber insurer, and an OFAC sanctions check before any payment
The group must run at least one cross-division exercise each year that includes OT isolation, the notification matrix, and a materiality decision
Reconnection
Evidence must be preserved with chain of custody, including controller logic and HMI state where it can be captured safely
A lessons-learned review must be completed within 30 days of recovery, and the risk registers, POA&M, and this policy updated
All information must be classified as Restricted, Confidential, Internal, or Public
Each division must keep an inventory of where Restricted and Confidential data is stored, including exports and copies
Restricted data must stay in approved systems
Restricted and Confidential data must be encrypted at rest and in transit wherever the system supports it
OT Confidential data (diagrams, rules, backups, vendor access details) may be shared with suppliers only under contract and need to know, and must...
The hazmat security plan may be shared only with employees who implement it and with authorized DOT or DHS officials on request
Media and records containing Restricted or Confidential data must be destroyed by shredding or erasure that makes the data unreadable (NIST SP...
Data must be retained under the group retention schedule and any longer regulatory period, and disposed of at the end of it unless on legal hold
Every workforce member must acknowledge these rules at hire and every year, and complete annual security awareness training
Only group-managed devices may connect to OT networks
Removable media may be used with OT only after a scan at a group scanning kiosk
Only approved software may be installed
Suspected phishing must be reported with the report button; never forward it
Photographs or screenshots of control room displays, OT network diagrams, or security plans must not be shared outside the group or on social media
Generative AI
Driver monitoring data (telematics, ELD, and camera data) may be used only for safety, compliance, and security purposes in the division...
Field logic changes need an approved change request before the change (emergency changes recorded within 24 hours)
Alarm-loss procedure: when SCADA alarms are lost at a battery using the SPCC high-level sensor option, shut in or start gauging rounds within 4 hours
Models or analytics may write to field devices only after council approval and safety management of change
Mid-Continent interim rules until migration: integrator access only through PAM; logs to the SIEM; offline backups
CIP-003-9 low impact plans: Sections 1 to 6 per asset group, approved by the CIP Senior Manager every 15 calendar months
Third-party transient cyber assets reviewed and recorded on the checklist before every connection
Vendor remote access only through group PAM with OT sensor rules for malicious communications
EOP-004 Operating Plan with offline contacts; CIP-012-2 plan for GCC data links
Loss or manipulation of SCADA is an abnormal operating condition in controller roles and training
Backup SCADA test every calendar year within 15 months; OT DMZ and jump server changes go through control room change management
Hazmat security plan includes cyber threats to dispatch, run tickets, and telematics; staff trained within 90 days of each plan revision
Driver camera AI scores reviewed by a person before any discipline
